Subject: Packaging questions — upgrade path and bundling

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team enjoyed seeing the Dedicated throughput metrics. We have a few open questions as we consider moving from the hosted tier to a reserved/dedicated plan:

- If we commit to Dedicated for 6 months vs 12 months, how does that affect available feature bundling (e.g., private VPC, extended retention, per-route tracing)?
- Can we temporarily burst to Dedicated during month-end processing without a full-term migration?
- What does a downgrade look like if our demand normalizes after the pilot?

We have a procurement review next Wednesday; it would be helpful to have a simple breakdown (recommended plan, short/medium term upgrade steps, and any one-time credits you can offer).

Hi Emma — great to hear from you and thanks for the usage file. Quick summary up front: we recommend a two-phase approach (Pilot -> Reserved Dedicated) with an interim burst plan for month-end spikes.

High-level recommendation:
- Phase 1 (Pilot, 1 month): Keep hosted for dev/staging and run a dedicated pilot pool (1x T4/Tesla equivalent) for production-critical endpoints. This avoids immediate commit and lets us validate latency/SLOs.
- Phase 2 (Commit, 6–12 months): Move mission-critical routes to a Dedicated pool. 12-month commit unlocks better unit pricing and feature bundles (VPC, longer audit log retention, and priority support).

Downgrade / rollback notes:
- We support rolling back routes to hosted variants; traffic routing rules are per-route and can be toggled in the Console. Reservations are time-bound — prorated refunds are not typical, but we can offer step-down grace credits for 6 -> 3 month changes within the first 90 days of a 12-month commit.

Attachments I’m including: a cleaned pricing worksheet with suggested tier (crestline_pricing_v1.xlsx) and a short migration playbook (redwood_migration_playbook.pdf).

Next steps I need from you:
1) Confirm 3–6 routes you want to pilot and expected QPS per route.
2) Share procurement contact and cadence (if procurement needs a formal MA or SOW).
3) Let me know if a one-time onboarding credit would help your procurement timeline.

I’ll copy Ben on the pricing specifics and Kimberly on the migration constraints.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Thanks Rachel — adding details on pricing concessions and approvals.

Pricing/concession summary:
- Standard 6-month Dedicated commit: 12% off published reserved rates.
- Standard 12-month Dedicated commit: 18% off.
- Up to 25% discount can be approved by Sales Leadership for strategic accounts with ARR > $250k — anything above 20% requires an exec review.
- We can provide a one-time onboarding credit (applies against first invoice) up to $25k for pilots that convert to 12-month commits within 45 days of pilot completion.

For procurement paperwork: we typically send an amendment + the standard T&Cs. If you need an accelerated approval path, I can route a concession term sheet to our legal team after you confirm the target discount.

I’ve attached a term sheet draft for the onboarding credit and concession framework (concession_term_sheet.pdf).

Hi Emma — a few technical clarifications to make sure the plan is executable: 

1) Burst to Dedicated
- We can configure a burst window (short lived) where selected routes are routed to Dedicated for up to 72 hours without a full commit, subject to capacity availability. Burst windows are billed at Dedicated rates; they don’t require contract changes but need scheduling 48 hours in advance for guaranteed capacity.

2) Feature bundling by commit length
- Hosted: base features (streaming, basic observability).
- Dedicated 6mo: adds isolated GPU pool, 30-day trace retention, and configurable autoscaling policies.
- Dedicated 12mo: additionally includes VPC peering, 90-day audit logs, dedicated on-call escalation, and priority kernel tuning availability.

3) Downgrade mechanics
- Route-level toggles preserve KV caches for 24 hours to reduce cold-starts when rolling back to hosted variants; however, quantization/weights are model-variant specific and may need a warmup period.

Recommended migration sequence:
- Stage routes behind feature flag -> Canary to Dedicated pilot -> Scale pilot for 2 billing cycles -> Convert to committed Dedicated (if metrics stable) -> Schedule a 30-day follow-up for retention/observability tuning.

If you’re open to it, I can book a 30–45 minute migration walkthrough with our SRE team and provide a tentative cron for burst windows.

-Kim
